q: How different is the energy use of a parboiled rice mill and a hulling-only mill?
title: Parboiled vs hulling rice mill: energy
short: Roughly 25 times. In Red Hills, a medium parboiled mill uses 384 toe a year, mostly husk or wood for steam, plus 545,460 kWh. A hulling unit that only removes husk and polishes uses 180,000 kWh, 15 toe, about 40 kWh per tonne of rice. Soaking, steaming and drying make the gap.
audience: Parboiled rice mills and hulling units in Red Hills, Chennai, and similar Tamil Nadu clusters

p: A Red Hills parboiled mill cleans paddy, soaks it about 4 hours in pits holding about 8 t each, steams it in 600 to 700 kg batches, then dries it from about 32% moisture to 22% and on to 13 to 14% over about 30 hours, before milling. A hulling unit skips soaking, steaming and drying and sends cleaned paddy straight to milling. Hulling units run round the clock for about three months, making raw rice for government programmes.

ul: Medium parboiled, 4 tph, 40 units: 545,460 kWh and 384 toe a year; electricity is about 12% of its energy.
Small parboiled, 3 tph, 30 units: 109,092 kWh and 110 toe a year.
Hulling, 3 tph, 30 units: 180,000 kWh and 15 toe a year, all electricity; about 40 kWh per tonne of rice, 0.003 toe.
Parboiled units overall: 0.061 to 0.064 toe per tonne. Milling alone draws 6.5 to 7 kWh per 75 kg bag of paddy.

sections.h: The dryer is the big steam user
p: About 80% of a parboiled mill's steam goes to the dryer, where steam heats air through a heat exchanger. TERI costed a husk fired hot air generator for a medium mill burning 1,120 t of husk, 900 t of it for drying: 28% saved, about 250 t of husk, Rs 5 lakh a year for Rs 5.5 lakh, payback about a year. The boiler can then shrink to about 1 tph, for parboiling only.

ul: Economiser and condensate return: 112 t of husk a year for Rs 1 lakh, payback about 5 months.
Combustion air control, against the unburnt husk and black smoke many boilers show: 60 t a year for Rs 0.7 lakh, payback about 7 months.

p: A parboiled mill's fossil CO2 is its power bill; the husk is biogenic and reported apart, though its methane and nitrous oxide count. A hulling unit's footprint is almost all grid power, so kWh per tonne is the whole story.

example.title: Per mill, per year (estimate)
lines: Medium parboiled: 545,460 kWh x 0.675 kg = 368 t fossil CO2
Medium parboiled husk: (384 toe minus 47 toe of power) x 41.868 GJ x 100 kg = about 1,410 t biogenic
Small parboiled: 109,092 kWh x 0.675 = 74 t fossil
Hulling: 180,000 kWh x 0.675 = 122 t fossil; 40 kWh x 0.675 = 27 kg per tonne of rice
example.note: Unit figures from TERI's Red Hills profile (2014-15). Biogenic CO2 uses the IPCC 2006 default for solid biomass; grid factor from CEA for FY 2025-26.

senseible: Senseible reads your electricity bills into monthly kWh and CO2 at the CEA factor, which for a hulling unit is nearly the whole footprint, and keeps husk bills in the same record for a parboiled mill.
